rows.name: dir?
rows.notes: Not defaulted, deliberately: left unset the resolved page direction governs, so a subtree inside an RTL region inherits instead of being reset to `ltr`.

rows.name: value?
rows.notes: Controlled. `null` is a value — it means no tab is selected.

rows.name: disabled?
rows.notes: The whole tab list. Individual tabs disable themselves on the trigger.

rows.name: closable?
rows.notes: Opens the close trigger, the `Delete` key and the middle click.

rows.name: lazyMount?
rows.notes: A panel does not exist until its tab has been activated once.

rows.name: keepMounted?
rows.notes: A panel stays rendered, `hidden`, after it is deactivated.

rows.name: scrollActiveIntoView?
rows.notes: Brings the selected tab back into view when the list overflows.

rows.name: describedBy?
rows.notes: Ids of the text describing this control — a `field` supplies them.

rows.name: intents?
rows.notes: Where LB/RB arrive from. `null` when the app runs no input system.

rows.name: onClose?
rows.notes: The consumer removes the tab; the machine only says which one and moves on.

rows.name: content?
rows.notes: The panel's content. A tab with an empty panel still has one to point at.

rows.name: disabled?
rows.notes: This tab alone. The whole list is disabled by `disabled` on the root.

rows.name: trigger?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY tab, hence no `value`, `label` or `disabled` — the entry's own fields, already excluded through `Own` — and no `id` **or IDREF**: one id repeated down a list is a broken reference per tab, and one `aria-labelledby` repeated gives every tab the same name, which no dangling-IDREF check can see because the id it points at does resolve. `aria-controls` goes with them for a sharper reason than the others: the machine writes it only where the panel it names is provably in the same markup (`ssr.test.tsx:494-496`), and a fixed one here would undo exactly that guarantee. `ref` goes because a single ref held by N tabs ends up holding the last one.

rows.name: closeTrigger?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY close button, and excluded for the same reasons. The `Own` parameter is not decoration here: `<button>` has a DOM attribute called `value`, typed `string | number | readonly string[]`, and without it the hatch would widen the part's own `value: string` — a spread applied last wins on the type as well as at runtime.

rows.name: content?
rows.notes: Applied to EVERY panel, and excluded for the same reasons.
